title: Show blocked availability on the calendar in View mode, not only Manage-availability mode
tech: React + TypeScript frontend only -- no backend change, the availability-exceptions API already exists and is already used in Manage mode
keyConstraints: Confirmed by reading frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.tsx in full: blocked availability_exceptions are currently only fetched once (mode === 'manage' && !exceptionsRequestedRef.current) -- the fetch effect (lines 258-287) and the exception-events memo (lines 294-299, `if (mode !== 'manage' || !exceptions) return [];`) both gate entirely on Manage mode. This was a deliberate decision in task 020, justified specifically to keep View mode's network behavior (and its existing tests) identical to what task 018 shipped -- not because visibility was considered undesirable. Found via live testing: this means a masseur in the default View mode cannot see their own blocked-out time at all, only bookings -- a real usability gap now that it's in use. Fix: fetch exceptions unconditionally on mount (same pattern as the existing bookings fetch effect, lines 226-253), and include exception-events in the merged events regardless of mode. Do NOT change the block-creation interaction (selectable={mode === 'manage'} and onSelectSlot gated to Manage mode, line 483-484) -- tapping empty calendar space to create a new block must remain Manage-mode-only; this task is only about making EXISTING blocks visible in View mode, not about letting View mode create them. Real design question for Architect, not a pure bug fix: handleSelectEvent's exception branch (line 312-319) currently calls handleUnblock(event.exception) immediately and unconditionally whenever a blocked-exception event is tapped -- with exceptions now visible in View mode too, this would let a masseur unblock a day from View mode, which defeats the purpose of Manage-availability mode existing as a distinct, deliberate mode for exactly this kind of mutation (contrast with task 022's booking actions, which were deliberately made mode-independent because they're unrelated to what the toggle is for -- blocking/unblocking IS what the toggle is for, so the same reasoning doesn't carry over automatically). Architect should propose and justify the View-mode tap behavior (e.g. show a small read-only detail instead of unblocking, or simply no-op) rather than silently keeping the existing immediate-unblock behavior active in View mode by default. This task will require updating existing AdminCalendar.test.tsx assertions that currently assert no exceptions fetch happens in View mode (task 020's added test) -- unlike the recent pure-CSS tasks, this is a genuine behavior change and those tests must be consciously updated to match the new intended behavior, not left broken or silently deleted.
description: Make blocked availability_exceptions visible on the calendar's grid in View mode (the default), not only after switching into Manage-availability mode. The masseur should be able to see their own blocked-out time at a glance without needing to enter the mode meant for creating/removing blocks. Block-creation (tapping empty space) stays Manage-mode-only. What happens when an already-visible blocked event is tapped in View mode is an open design question for Architect to resolve -- see keyConstraints.
acceptanceCriteria: Blocked availability_exceptions are fetched on initial mount (same timing as the bookings fetch), not lazily deferred until Manage mode is entered
Blocked-exception events render on the calendar grid in View mode, visually distinguished the same way they already are in Manage mode
Tapping empty calendar space to create a new block remains impossible in View mode -- selectable/onSelectSlot stay gated to Manage mode only, unchanged
Tapping an already-blocked event in View mode does not silently trigger an unblock (immediate deletion) -- Architect's proposed alternative behavior is implemented and justified
Manage mode's existing tap-to-unblock behavior for blocked events is unchanged

Existing AdminCalendar.test.tsx assertions that assumed no exceptions fetch happens in View mode are consciously updated to reflect the new intended behavior, with reasoning for the change, not silently deleted or left failing
Layout/rendering verified at a narrow (phone-width) viewport, consistent with this project's established mobile-first requirement
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in frontend/ (backend should be unaffected since no backend files change)
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.tsx (the fetch effect, events memo, and handleSelectEvent -- the actual changes)
frontend/test/AdminCalendar.test.tsx (existing View-mode-fetch assertions must be found and consciously updated)
securityConsiderations: None -- blocked-exception data was already fully readable by any authenticated masseur session via Manage mode; this only changes when it's fetched/rendered, not who can see it.
